detail: Live on HEAD 3956cfb: initialize + tools/list via 4-byte BE length-prefixed framing (the MCP spec stdio transport, what real MCP clients use) → no response in 5s, process stays alive; same requests newline-delimited with stdin held open → both respond immediately (13 tools). The report's 'stdin-open hang' is the wrong mechanism — framing is the blocker; EOF-piped and newline-delimited stdin-open both work.
foreman_note: Measured with bin/crier-mcp built from d337b3f: a 4-byte big-endian length-prefixed initialize frame gets an immediate JSON-RPC response {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32700,"message":"parse error"},"id":null} and the process exits 0 with stdin closed — not the 'no response in 5s, process stays alive' the row states. The silence it saw is NDJSON waiting for a line terminator while stdin is held open with no newline; newline-delimited framing IS the MCP stdio transport framing, so crier is spec-conformant. A future docs tick may add one line to README saying so, but there is no defect to fix.

detail: Deep-debug audit 2026-09-14: the two hottest events on a message bus — a relay publish accepted and a webhook delivery dispatched — emit ZERO log lines (internal/relay/handler.go: 0 slog calls; internal/webhook/driver.go: 0). There is no request correlation id (X-Request-Id or otherwise), so a 202 in the access log cannot be tied to the later webhook POST, guard decision, or FEDERATION_FAILED notice. Federation is the counter-example: hold.go logs the entire lifecycle (held, retry-persist, recovered, failed) and it is a joy to debug. Fix: (1) middleware generates/propagates X-Request-Id, echoes it on responses, and every slog line in the request path carries it; (2) deliver-202, webhook dispatch + outcome, and guard decision log one line each carrying message_id + agent_id + sender; (3) mesh REGISTER/REQUEST-drop and WS subscribe/unsubscribe lifecycle log at debug level.

detail: Worker out-of-scope finding during DF-CRIER-151 (worker c319e6f, live postgres probe /tmp/crier-t268/probe-out.txt): the PATCH /agents/{id} response echoes the PRE-write last_seen. detail: CI run 35038607923 (push of board commit 3c0242c) failed Build & Test on internal/registry: TestDeliver_Blocking_TimeoutIs504/endpoint_hangs_past_the_budget got status=200 body={"id":"...","transport":"webhook","reply":""} instead of the expected 504. The endpoint sleeps 2s, budget is 100ms, so the first attempt should time out and DeliverBlocking should return the 'timed out' error -> 504. A 200 with an empty reply means c.http.Do returned a completed (empty-body) 2xx within the budget, i.e. the client's http.Client.Timeout cut the hanging attempt even though cfg.TimeoutMs=100 was far below the next retry's needs. Foreman repro: passes -count=8 (residue), then 20/20 isolated subtest and 30/30 full-package after go clean -testcache (58/58 total) on this host. Code read: webhook.Client has a DRIVER-GLOBAL timeout (NewClient(timeout, secret)); the blocking attempt request carries NO per-attempt context deadline (postBody builds without ctx), so per-attempt waits rely on the global client timeout only; handler.go:590 maps req.TimeoutMs->budget=100ms correctly. Also verify whether deliverHarness's TimeoutMs:100 override reaches the client (webhook.Config.TimeoutMs) or only sets the budget. Fix candidates: (a) give the blocking attempt context.WithTimeout(remaining budget) so an attempt can never overrun the budget; (b) harden the test (longer hang, wall-clock assert); (c) check no package-level shared webhook.Client with a short timeout bleeds across tests in the same package. Evidence trail: tick 271 audit event 451; gh run 35038607923 failed-step log; internal/webhook/driver.go DeliverBlocking; internal/webhook/webhook.go postBody; internal/registry/handler.go:590.

Fix is in the production path (no test was weakened). Semantics preserved: ctx deadline stays Retryable -> 504, non-retryable rejections and unmappable 2xx stay ErrPermanent -> 502.

detail: A header-logging sink recorded X-Crier-Agent: alice (the deliver body's sender; empty when sender is omitted) and the envelope body carries no target at all, while specs/WEBHOOK-DELIVERY.md:56 documents X-Crier-Agent as {target_agent_id} — a sink author cannot identify which agent a delivery is for. The fix keeps X-Crier-Agent as the sender (its real, long-standing meaning) and makes the target identifiable additively: a new X-Crier-Target header and crier.target envelope field name the agent the delivery is FOR, and a blank X-Crier-Agent is no longer sent at all. Separately, examples/demo.sh's keyless-guard note claimed an inbox delivery is flagged X-Crier-Guard-Error: true — that header exists only on the outbound webhook POST, so the note now says the verdict rides in the deliver response body (README:243/516 and integration-guide:64 were already correctly scoped).

detail: internal/registry/remote.go:245-255 List swallows EVERY decode error: `if err := s.do(http.MethodGet, "/agents", nil, &out); err != nil { return []*Agent{} }`. A decode failure, a 401/403 and a 5xx are therefore all indistinguishable from an EMPTY REGISTRY on the bridge surface, and the failure is silent (no log, no error returned to the caller). DF-CRIER-198 (c4f2f04) removed the one trigger that existed at the time - a keyless agent whose empty public_key failed HexKey.UnmarshalJSON - by making the decode accept the empty key; the pattern that turned that decode failure into a confident zero-agent answer is untouched, so the NEXT decode regression (schema drift on Agent, a new field, a changed wire shape) will be reported to an MCP bridge as `{"agents":[]}` instead of as an error. Reproduce at c4f2f04: point a RemoteStore at a server that answers /agents with a shape it cannot decode (or with a 500) and observe List() returning an empty slice with no error and no log line. Acceptance: RemoteStore.List stops laundering failures into an empty slice - either the decode error is surfaced to the caller (an error return, or a distinguishable sentinel) or it is at minimum logged once per occurrence with the status/body context, while a genuinely empty registry still returns an empty slice; an erroring server must be distinguishable from an empty one by a bridge caller, and focused tests cover both the empty-registry case and the undecodable-response case. Filed from the DF-CRIER-198 worker's out-of-scope report; premise re-verified by the foreman at c4f2f04 by reading remote.go:245-255.

detail: ROOT CAUSE of the 2026-09-18 host lock-up (Bane: 'another one of those fork bombs'). The DF-CRIER-252-class repro ('test fails 4/24 runs ON A LOADED BOX') drives a load generator that spawns unbounded busy-wait units: `timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c while :; do :; done`, launched from a `for i in $(seq ...)` loop in /home/kara/crier. MEASURED: 73 -> 278 concurrent units over ~20 min; each burns ~13% CPU (null loop, zero work); combined with the fleet, loadavg hit 220/346/237 with ~2000 processes; the box was effectively unusable for hours. Repeated judge runs (gitreins task complete DF-CRIER-252, judge --run-job job-1b252442...) respawn them, and units are ORPHANED to `systemd --user` (PPID=user manager) when their spawner exits, so they outlive the evaluation that created them (300s lifetime each, unbounded count). No containment existed: user-manager TasksMax=72934 (effectively unlimited). FIX: (1) bound the load in the repro harness - hard max unit count (default <=8), unit lifetime <=30s, try/finally + SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP teardown so no unit outlives its run; (2) never leave orphans: the harness must kill its own process group on exit and on abort; (3) serialize load-class work - one load repro at a time per host, and skip (recorded as SKIPPED with reason) when host loadavg is already above threshold; (4) prefer a bounded load tool over hand-rolled while-loops. FLEET MITIGATION INSTALLED (Kara-agent): ~/.hermes/scripts/forkbomb-reaper.py + forkbomb-reaper.timer (60s) kills busy-wait units older than 120s and logs to ~/.hermes/logs/forkbomb-reaper.jsonl; first run reaped 49 units + their spawner. PENDING (needs root): TasksMax/MemoryMax drop-in on user@1000.service as structural containment.  CORRECTION (same day, after reading the code): `scripts/loadgen.py` is NOT the emitter — it is the already-correct replacement (bounded workers MAX_WORKERS=8, capped seconds, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG so children die with the runner, refuses to run on a shared host, fails the run if any child survives). The actual emitter is AD-HOC, AGENT-AUTHORED shell: agents hand-rolled `for i in $(seq 1 N); do timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c 'while :; do :; done' & done` as a 'load the box' step, with no teardown, so the units were orphaned to systemd --user and outlived every caller (state.db evidence across projects/weeks: Kobayashi-Maru 2026-08-25, ring-runner, crier). FIX LANDED 2026-09-18: the terminal-jail plugin now vetoes this class at the tool boundary (pre_tool_call block directive) via terminal_jail/spin_policy.py — busy-wait loops, unbounded yes/cat /dev/zero/dd burns and shell fork bombs; 5/5 tests pass; deliberate override HERMES_TERMINAL_JAIL_ALLOW_SPIN=1. Remaining scope: make loadgen the easy path for agents (wrapper + AGENTS.md pointer), audit remaining harnesses for the old idiom, keep the host reaper as backstop. NOTE: this row was lost once to a mid-write crash during that same correction pass and restored from HEAD~1 (see commit message).  ROOT CAUSE FOUND (code level, 2026-09-18 evening): the emitter is GitReins' OWN tier-2 evaluator. `engine/evaluator.py::_tool_run_command` ran the judge's shell as `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, timeout=...)` — `timeout=` reaps only the DIRECT child, so any BACKGROUNDED children escape: a command like `for i in $(seq 1 64); do timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c 'while :; do :; done' & done` (the idiom the judge invents when a criterion demands 'fails on a loaded box') leaves every unit running, reparented to `systemd --user`. Measured: 278 orphans, loadavg 220-346. ps chain proved the path: `gitreins task complete DF-CRIER-252` → the for-loop shell → the burners (a direct child of the gitreins process, which is why no Hermes session/tool-call record exists and why the terminal-jail veto does NOT cover it — the host reaper was the only backstop). Amplifiers: the tier-2 stage is budgeted at 400 iterations / 30m / 48M input tokens (crier/.gitreins/config.yaml), so a judge run is long and can issue many commands; crier's own criteria (e.g. QA-CRIER-17: '20+ consecutive go test ./cmd/server -count=1 runs are green') legitimately push the judge toward load-bearing verification. FIX LANDED: new `engine/command_hygiene.py` — (a) refuses busy-wait/unbounded-burn/fork-bomb commands with a message naming `sleep` and `scripts/loadgen.py`; (b) spawns every command with `start_new_session=True` and reaps the WHOLE process group on timeout AND on normal exit (validated pgid: never PID 1, group must exist in /proc, survivors are reported in the tool result rather than hidden). Wired into `_tool_run_command` and `pipeline._run_script_step`. Tests: `tests/test_command_hygiene.py`, 20 passing behaviour tests (backgrounded child reaped on normal exit; timeout kills the group; refusal proven by side effect). Deploy step: the lanes run the pipx copy at ~/.local/share/pipx/venvs/gitreins (installed from file:///home/kara/gitreins-poc), so it must be reinstalled from the repo for the fix to reach them.

detail: Measured 2026-09-18/19 (tick 342). bunker-e2e run 35408229089 (headSha 0914766, a board-JSONL-only commit — the diff cannot affect a container deploy) failed in job 'Bunker config-matrix E2E', step 'Deploy container to bunker + run config-matrix battery', during cell 'guard-on (default guard, real deepseek)' after `preflight OK`. Sequence from the log: image tarball -> bunker transport retried and succeeded ('attempt 1/4 (retry budget 3) -- OK'), 'docker load on <host>' retried and succeeded, THEN `bunker: stream error: deadline_exceeded: context deadline exceeded`, and the enclosing 'cell deploy: guard-on' leg reported: 'attempt 1/4 (retry budget 3 not spent — not retryable) — NON_TRANSPORT (exit 1; not a transport signature, output: sha256:74a271eae952015703d5a08ed369d74d501e977fe38a4a2d70682e78278fcfc4)' followed by FATAL. So a transport-shaped failure (a stream deadline) was classified NON_TRANSPORT, the budget of 3 retries was left UNSPENT, and the job died on the first attempt. The captured 'output' the classifier judged is the image sha256 line — the real signature ('deadline_exceeded', 'stream error') was on the line just before it, i.e. the classifier is reading the wrong line (or the wrong stream) of a multi-line attempt, so any cell deploy whose failure text is a stream error is unretryable. This is a follow-on to INT-CI-001 (commit 65aa127), which added exactly this retry+classify leg for the ssh/scp reset case and is complete — the classifier's signature set is what is incomplete, not the retry loop. detail: FOUND BY DOGFOOD 2026-09-23 (real-use run, docs/dogfood/2026-09-23-real-use.md). The openai-compatible template renders its outbound body from a HARD-CODED shape (internal/webhook/schema.go:55-81): {"model":"{{agent.model|default:deepseek-v4-flash}}", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"{{payload.text}}"}]}. A payload with no `text` key renders the content field EMPTY (expandTemplate substitutes the empty string, it does not fail), the webhook POST goes out with content:"", the endpoint answers 200, and crier reports the delivery as successful. MEASURED live, same relay, same endpoint, payload shape the only variable: payload {"task":"held work"} -> reply "echo: " (200, transport webhook); payload {"text":"dogfood hello over federation"} -> reply "echo: dogfood hello over federation". title: [P2] Declare the auth reality: what a spec-generated (bearer-only) Muster client can and cannot drive, so nobody hits an unexplained 401.
detail: crier declares bearerAuth (global) AND agentSignature. title: [P3] A2A task lifecycle (GetTask / ListTasks / CancelTask) mapped onto the inbox entry + lease/ack.
detail: A2A is task-oriented: Task with TaskState, and GetTask (GET /tasks/{id}), ListTasks (GET /tasks), CancelTask (POST /tasks/{id}:cancel), SubscribeToTask (POST /tasks/{id}:subscribe). title: [P1] Mesh carries NO authentication — identity is the URL path only, so any network-reachable client can impersonate an agent on the lateral-movement lane (external review #1).
detail: Carter's #1 finding, VERIFIED at HEAD 0b60acc: `grep -rnE 'requireAgent|Signature|token|auth' internal/mesh/*.go` returns ZERO hits. `/mesh/connect/{agentID}` proves nothing about the caller — the agent id is a PATH CLAIM, not an identity — while crier's registry holds an ed25519 key per agent and enforces it on the inbox lane. Net effect: the one lane built for agent-to-agent request/response is the one lane where a compromised or hostile peer can speak as anyone, and the review reports the origin policy is allow-all by default. HONEST FRAMING: this is documented-by-design in docs/mesh-protocol.md, not a silent defect — but it is the biggest verified hole for any multi-agent or shared deployment, because it bypasses the identity story crier advertises. ACCEPTANCE (one of, chosen in the spec): an ed25519 challenge on connect, per-frame signatures, or a session token issued at connect and required on frames; PLUS the origin policy made explicit and configurable rather than allow-all. Do NOT silently tighten the default in a way that breaks existing single-host deployments — ship it behind the documented config with a migration note. Evidence owed: a frame from an unauthenticated peer rejected, and an authenticated one accepted, captured live. title: [P2] Finish task ownership: sender idempotency keys, a dead-letter queue, TTL-expiry receipts, and transfer/reassign.
detail: The review's 'the lease is the lock' section is right and VERIFIED: `grep -i idempot internal/` finds only Start/Stop comments — there is NO sender-supplied idempotency key, so a retried deliver duplicates work; TTL expiry purges silently with no notify path, so a sender never learns its work died; there is no transfer/reassign and no DLQ (only webhook BATCHES dead-letter on permanent 4xx — a precedent to copy, not a general mechanism). title: [P3] Guard verdict asymmetry past 64 KiB (+ the ±30s replay window) — two measured notes
foreman_note: tick 406 wave. Follow-up for the next README owner: README lines ~1207/1549 describe the over-cap allow without naming errored:true (sibling-owned file this tick).
reasoning:
BOTH ARE NOTES FROM the independent QA re-run (CRI-001-R2), kept because each is a
measured surprise rather than a style opinion. Neither is a crash; both are traps for
whoever builds on the verdict.

NOTE 1 (X9) — GUARD VERDICT ASYMMETRY ABOVE 64 KiB. A payload past the guard cap gets
regex-only classification and returns `reason:"payload_exceeds_guard_cap: low-confidence
prematch only", errored:false` — the LLM is never consulted. So an attacker who pads the
body and phrases the injection to MISS the regexes receives a clean ALLOW with
errored:false, a STRONGER-LOOKING verdict than the errored verdict a SMALL payload gets.
The prematch still blocks high-confidence patterns (a padded "ignore all previous
instructions" is 403 GUARD_BLOCKED), so this is a gap in the corpus, not an open door —
but the verdict is less trustworthy exactly where the payload is least inspectable.

NOTE 2 (X3) — A REPLAYED SIGNATURE IS ACCEPTED INSIDE THE ±30 s WINDOW. The pass recorded
a byte-identical signed request replayed inside the freshness window and accepted. This is
the documented trade (the window IS the freshness mechanism, and the same pass measured
stale/future timestamps -> 401), so it is a NOTE, not a FAIL — but the ±30 s window is the
whole replay defence on those routes.

ACCEPTANCE (either): (a) past the cap, return a verdict that cannot read as a confident
allow (e.g. errored:true + reason, or an explicit oversized_payload classification), with a
test that pads an injection to miss the regexes and asserts the verdict is not a clean
allow; and (b) document the ±30 s replay window in README/mesh docs as the replay defence,
or add a nonce/cache so a byte-identical replay inside the window is refused. If (b) is
judged out of scope, say so in the row's close note rather than leaving it implied.

title: [P1] Agent classes & resource ownership: personal vs service/shared agents, agents that OWN systems/code, default cross-owner denial
reasoning:
Bane, 2026-10-03: two classes of agent, with different permissions by construction.

PERSONAL agent — owned by one human; it knows about its owner (a private context about me); default reach = its owner plus explicitly granted principals. This is my agent, I talk to it.

SERVICE / SHARED agent — scoped; may OWN systems, code or other things (an agent that owns a repo, a box, a service). It is reachable according to its scope, not its owner.

THE RULE THAT MATTERS: the permission model must let me talk to MY agents but NOT to YOURS — cross-owner is default-deny, and reaching another owner's agent requires an explicit grant (or its declaration as a service agent whose scope includes me).

So this row defines the taxonomy (class), the OWNER relation, the OWNS/SCOPE relation over resources (systems, code, other things), and the default-reachability matrix per class. CR-CHAT-003 (roles + grants) and CR-CHAT-007 (human identity) build ON this taxonomy, so it is filed first.

ACCEPTANCE: the class + ownership model is normative; the default-reachability matrix is stated per class and tested (my agent: reachable by me, refused to a stranger; your agent: refused to me without a grant; a service agent with a scope: reachable per scope, with the scope itself an explicit, inspectable object).

title: [P1] Message kinds: a plain message vs an ADDRESSED message vs a TASK/ACTION — a tag is addressing, NEVER an instruction to execute or a fan-out
reasoning:
Bane, 2026-10-03: 'if you tag an agent with a message that doesn't go to other agents as an action to execute'.

So a TAG is ADDRESSING, not a command. Tagging an agent says 'this message is for you'; it does NOT mean 'execute this', and it does NOT fan out to other agents as a task for them.

DESIGN: distinguish message KINDS explicitly, because they carry different obligations and must be structurally distinguishable on the wire, in storage, and in the transcript:
  (1) PLAIN MESSAGE   — a message in a thread, visible to the thread's participants. No obligation.
  (2) ADDRESSED MESSAGE — '@agent' inside a message. The tagged participant is the intended reader. Others still see it per the thread's own rules. NOTHING EXECUTES. This is the default meaning of a tag.
  (3) TASK / ACTION   — the explicit 'do this' construct: the ONLY kind that may create work, carry a lifecycle (claimed/running/done/failed), and be addressed to a capability or group for execution. Must be rendered differently and stored as its own kind.

WHY IT MATTERS: conflating (2) and (3) is how a chat with agents becomes a system that silently does things — a tag would become a remote command, and an addressed reply would fan out to strangers. Keeping them distinct is the safety property.

ACCEPTANCE: tagging an agent produces an ADDRESSED MESSAGE and nothing executes and no third party receives a task; a task exists only via the explicit action kind; the two are visibly and structurally distinguishable in the transcript, on the wire, and in the JSONL record.

title: [P1] Federation AUTH — replace the single shared secret with a real peer-auth process (peer identity, mutual auth, per-peer authorization, revocation)

Bane, 2026-10-03: 'federation between criers with an auth process'.

THE PROBLEM, MEASURED: the ONLY federation credential today is ONE shared secret (CR_FED_TOKEN; the source's CR_FED_TOKEN equals the destination's CR_AUTH_TOKEN). Every peer shares it. title: [P1] Chain of trust / signing trusts — turn the existing ed25519 message auth + hash-chained delivery log into a real trust model
reasoning:
Bane, 2026-10-03: 'chain of trust, since we are already doing some auth for messages we need to allow signing trusts'.

WHAT EXISTS (grounded, not invented): every agent holds an ed25519 key and every delivery passes through it; the OPT-IN delivery log is hash-chained — each record carries prev_hash naming its predecessor whose value is inside the hash — and the record is signed by the server's ed25519 key (specs/DETECTION.md). The spec itself says of the detection layer: 'wiring, not a new trust primitive'. The primitives therefore exist; the TRUST MODEL does not.

OWED: WHO VOUCHES FOR A KEY and how a verifier decides to believe a signature it has never seen before. Concretely: a key may be signed by another key (a delegation), an instance may publish or accept a peer's key set, and a verifier walks that chain to a trust ANCHOR it already holds. Plus: KEY ROTATION without breaking history, and REVOCATION with a stated consequence for already-signed records.

THE HARD QUESTION TO ANSWER IN THE SPEC, not to hand-wave: what does trust do to a record that was valid when signed and whose key is revoked later? The hash chain makes history immutable, so revocation cannot rewrite it — the model must say what a revoked-but-chained record MEANS.

ACCEPTANCE: a signed message from an untrusted-but-vouched key verifies via a chain to a held anchor; a key with no path to an anchor is refused with a NAMED error; rotating a key keeps the chain verifiable; revoking a key is visible and its meaning for old records is stated; and the whole thing is testable from a fixture chain.

title: [P2] The per-agent signature does not bind the BODY — a signed message is not a claim this system can make today
reasoning:
FOUND while writing specs/CHAT-TRUST.md, and VERIFIED at the source (not inferred).

WHAT SHIPS: an agent's request carries X-Agent-ID, X-Agent-Ts and X-Agent-Sig, and the signature is ed25519 over the string METHOD + newline + path + newline + ts. Code: internal/registry/remote.go:98 builds exactly that payload; internal/registry/agentsig.go:37 documents it (path is the decoded URL path, query excluded). So the signature proves the key holder sent a request to THAT PATH at THAT TIME.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not bind the message BODY. A body can be swapped between a signed request and the delivery it causes, inside the plus-or-minus 30 second window, and the signature still verifies.

WHY IT MATTERS: Bane asked for signing trusts on the footing that crier is already doing some auth for messages. That is only half true — the SERVER signs content in the opt-in hash-chained detection log (the record hash covers the body), but the AGENT signature covers the request line only. So trust in an agent's CONTENT is not currently expressible.

OWED: a canonical transcript that includes a digest of the payload (sha256), so a signature binds what was said and not only where it was sent. The design is proposed in CHAT-TRUST.md section 5.1 and open question 1.

ACCEPTANCE: a signed delivery whose body was altered after signing FAILS verification with a NAMED outcome; the existing request-line verification keeps working for callers that do not opt into body binding (extend, never replace).

title: [P2] Summary roll-up — summaries OF summaries, an agent summarising the summaries of other agents
reasoning:
Bane, 2026-10-03: 'sometimes you eventually want summaries of summaries — you want your agent to summarize everything, the summaries of all those other agents.'

WHAT IT IS: a hierarchical summarisation — one agent's summary rolls up the summaries produced by several other agents (or threads) into a single higher-level summary, and in principle that roll-up can itself be summarised a level up.

THE RULES THAT KEEP IT HONEST: a roll-up is GENERATED and marked as such; it CITES its constituent summaries (so a reader can walk down to any source), and it never becomes the record it summarises; the depth is bounded and stated (a reader must be able to tell a summary from a summary of summaries); and a missing constituent summary is a NAMED gap in the roll-up, not silently skipped.

THIS IS A NEW PRODUCER: someone (an agent) now writes summaries OF other agents' work. That is a trust/authority question as much as a UI one — a roll-up can only summarise what its author was permitted to read (CR-CHAT-003).

ACCEPTANCE: roll up the summaries of N agents into one, which cites each constituent; expanding a constituent resolves to that agent's summary and then to its trace; a constituent the summariser could not read appears as a named gap; and the roll-up is labelled as generated at every level.

title: [P1] Dagger as a SCHEDULING ENGINE for agent work — DAG nodes that drive crier, and crier events that trigger a DAG
reasoning:
Bane, 2026-10-03: 'also as a scheduling engine ... this way I script processes of the agents working hard.'

THE TWO DIRECTIONS: (a) INBOUND — a DAG node invokes crier: deliver a message to an agent and WAIT for that agent's reply or its ack before the next node, so a pipeline can script several agents working in sequence or in parallel and gather their outputs. (b) OUTBOUND — a crier event (a TASK created, an agent's reply, a threshold) triggers a DAG run.

WHY THIS IS THE POINT: it lets Bane SCRIPT the agents — a durable, resumable, observable process rather than a human nudging agents by hand. The DAG is the orchestration; crier is the transport and the record; neither replaces the other.

THE HARD PARTS TO SPEC, not to hand-wave: a node that waits on an agent must have a stated TIMEOUT and a stated outcome on expiry (a held delivery and a DAG node that never resolves are the same failure); the retry semantics of a crier delivery (idempotency keys) must compose with the DAG's own retry so an agent is not asked to do the same work twice; and a cancelled DAG must not leave an agent still working unawaited.

ACCEPTANCE: a two-node DAG delivers to agent A, waits for A's reply, then delivers to agent B with A's output; the run resumes from a checkpoint after a crash without re-delivering to A; a node whose agent never replies expires with a NAMED outcome and the run fails or branches accordingly; and a cancelled run leaves no agent still holding an unawaited task.

reasoning:
Bane, 2026-10-05: JSONL and SQLite support are important so a user does not have to run PostgreSQL.

CLARIFICATION TO CR-CHAT-006 / D6: JSONL remains the portable ordered append/interchange format. SQLite must be a FIRST-CLASS queryable and durable backend so a single-user/local deployment can run with no PostgreSQL service. PostgreSQL remains an optional server-backed backend for multi-user/scale deployments. Do not encode 'Postgres is the only queryable store' as a design constraint.

ARCHITECTURE REQUIREMENT: SQLite and PostgreSQL must share one storage/repository implementation and one Go database access API so supporting a second engine does not require rewriting or copying the session store. Recommended baseline: Go database/sql behind the session Store contract, PostgreSQL through the existing pgx database/sql adapter, and a pure-Go SQLite driver; keep only connection setup, dialect/migration details, and genuinely engine-specific operations in adapters. These are separate engine drivers behind the same API, not one identical low-level driver. A common ORM/query layer is acceptable only if it preserves the existing transaction, idempotency, and JSONL projection semantics.

OWED: config selection + migrations/schema for SQLite; the same session, membership, transcript, thread, task and asset-reference records as the PostgreSQL view; append/replay/reconcile behavior against JSONL; transactional/idempotent replay; backup/export/import; clear concurrency and locking behavior.

ACCEPTANCE: a clean install with only SQLite and JSONL can create a session, append and retrieve messages, branch a thread, restart, and recover identical state; the same portable bundle imports into SQLite and PostgreSQL with equivalent reads; parity tests cover append, duplicate replay, crash/restart and reconciliation; and no PostgreSQL URL/service is required for the SQLite path.

title: [P2] Task lifecycle re-proof (DF-CRIER-304 closed): READ/claim/complete/409-ladder all verified live — but the ADDRESSEE cannot act on the task addressed to him without class+owner scaffolding (docs teach the lifecycle nowhere)

title: [P3] Management surface is WRITE-ONLY: no GET on /principals, /bindings or /agents/{id}/class (405) — an operator cannot audit what he armed; JSONL store is the only reader
body: Real use 2026-10-13, HEAD 7c48745, port 18821: after minting 2 principals, 1 binding, 2 class records and a grant, GET /principals, GET /bindings and GET /agents/{id}/class all answer 405 method not allowed. Real workflow that dead-ends: 'what principals exist / what class is agent X / is this grant still live?' — every one needs a shell on the host. Fix direction: read routes on the management surface behind the SAME admin gate (GET /principals, GET /bindings, GET /agents/{id}/class, GET /grants — each a fold of the JSONL at current state), or at minimum document 'the JSONL under CR_PERMISSIONS_DIR is the only audit view' in the README ACL section so an operator knows before he arms.

title: [P3] CR_DATABASE_URL rejects the sqlite scheme with a postgres parse error naming 'sqlite:///...' verbatim — honest but confusing; and two identical-but-unknown request fields are handled with opposite strictness (sessions rejects 'name', /principals accepts an 'id')

Fix direction: (a) config-load hint naming the two env vars; (b) pick one unknown-field policy for management/session request bodies.

title: [P2] Preserve model/provider hints and authorized router inbox delivery for bunker dispatches
worker_summary: deepseek-v4-flash/deepseek-foreman worker (session 20261015_050403_52da62): optional model/provider selection hints + reply_to correlation on the inbox envelope; migration 013 (inbox_selection JSONB); canonical default = omitted member, Crier never fills a pair; signed-identity authorization, forged reply_to cannot grant authority; stub-router lease/reply/ack round trip + lease expiry/redelivery tested; docs/router-dispatch.md both modes + OpenAPI + claims. 15 new tests in crfeat036_test.go; full suite 28/28 ok; integration (testcontainers PG) ok; docs-check ok; guard PASS at 521257b.
reasoning:
Owner-confirmed architecture: the scheduler publishes a lane dispatch to Crier; Crier relays it to a bunker-local task-router inbox; that router interprets model/provider hints, selects an allowed model/provider pair from the prompt, and invokes the Hermes Gateway in its bunker; the correlated result returns through Crier to the scheduler. The bunker router polls Crier's inbox because the bunker does not accept inbound connections.

Crier's scope is transport, inbox delivery, authorization, and preserving optional selection hints—not prompt analysis, model/provider selection, Hermes execution, or scheduler pool/target setup. Keep both model and provider optional. Preserve explicit values unchanged so non-router consumers can select a model/provider without requiring a task-router. In router mode, do not replace default/unset values with a concrete Crier default: the task-router interprets them. Required selection cases for the consumer contract: (1) explicit model + explicit provider: use that pair; (2) default/unset model + explicit provider: select a model within that provider; (3) explicit model + default/unset provider: choose a compatible/best provider for that model; (4) both default/unset: choose the pair from the prompt. Define one canonical default representation while preserving supported null/blank forms. Do not add a scheduler task ID to the dispatch envelope; use Crier message/correlation identifiers.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Crier delivery tests prove explicit model/provider hints survive unchanged and default/unset/null/blank forms remain visible to a stub polling router; Crier never fills a concrete model or provider. Cover all four explicit/default combinations in the message contract.
2. Least-privilege service identities allow the scheduler to send to the intended router inbox and the router to return a correlated response to the scheduler; unrelated sender/recipient pairs are denied, and payload reply_to alone cannot grant authority.
3. The stub router retrieves/leases the scheduler message, returns a reply carrying the original Crier message correlation, and acknowledges only completed work; lease expiry/redelivery behavior remains intact.
4. Document both supported modes: explicit model/provider callers that do not use a task-router, and router-delegated selection when one or both hints are default/unset. Preserve existing inbox/delivery behavior for other consumers.

Non-goals: implement prompt-based model/provider selection or the Hermes Gateway call in Crier; those belong to the task-router/Gateway component. Implement scheduler target and usage-pool registration here; those belong to the scheduler.

title: [P1] Async webhook exhaustion is a silent drop when the deliver body omits sender — DF-CRIER-8 notification never fires (re-proof found the residual gap)
reasoning: Live re-proof of the DF-CRIER-8 fix at HEAD 839b4f2 (binary v0.1.0-rc2-409-g839b4f2). With a sender in the deliver body the exhaustion notification fires exactly as the spec promises (6s observed with redeliver=3s, budget=2; payload kind=error/code=WEBHOOK_FAILED/message_id/target/retries/status_code=500; ack ok). WITHOUT a sender field the driver logs 'webhook: failure notification skipped (no sender on exhausted item)' and the delivery is dropped with NO durable trace anywhere a user can see: sender inbox empty, no notification, only a WARN buried in server logs. Every real fire-and-forget caller that omits sender (the documented default — 'the server does not require or verify it') gets the exact silent drop DF-CRIER-8 was filed for. Fix direction: on exhaustion without sender, still write SOMETHING durable and user-visible — e.g. a WEBHOOK_FAILED notification into the TARGET agent's own inbox (the agent whose endpoint failed is the one whose operator must learn about it), or a server-level durable alert row; 'skip best-effort' should mean the notification write failed, not that there is nothing to notify. Spec §4 says 'A missing sender ... is logged best-effort' — the spec itself documents the gap; bring the spec and the behavior to a durable-outcome contract.

title: [P0] Session fan-out writes the inbox directly, bypassing the guard/webhook delivery path — a /chat send never reaches a harness
reasoning:
FOUND by the 2026-10-19 quorum (gpt-6.1-sol + grok-4.7 both flagged it; coordinator verified every line below).

WHAT THE CODE DOES: cmd/server/sessionroutes.go:72 wires NewHTTPHandler with `Deliverer: registryStore`, so internal/session/fanout.go:215 calls store.Deliver(target, entry) and internal/registry/memory_store.go appends to that agent's inbox. The guard choke point and the blocking webhook dispatch live in a DIFFERENT function — internal/registry/handler.go:1572-1634 (`h.guard.Check` at :1588) and :1675 — reached only by POST /agents/{id}/inbox.

WHY IT MATTERS: a session message can be recorded as "delivered" while no webhook consumer ever receives a hook. The ecosystem harnesses (claude-code, opencode, codex, pi-agent, aider, goose) consume via webhook/inbox HTTP, so the /chat surface and the harness path are two different roads. That makes the UI a transcript store, not a control panel, and it contradicts specs/CHAT-INTERFACE.md:85 which describes session fan-out as reusing "guard / webhook / durable write / lease / ack / TTL / dead-letter / federation fallback".

ACCEPTANCE: (1) session fan-out and POST /agents/{id}/inbox share ONE delivery service, so guard verdicts, webhook dispatch, lease/ack, dead-letter and federation fallback apply to session sends; (2) a message sent from /chat to a registered webhook agent produces an actual webhook POST (proven by a receiving stub) and its reply is visible in the original thread; (3) the transcript labels the outcome from the transport result, never from the store write; (4) a fan-out to an agent whose webhook fails is recorded as a failed delivery, not "delivered".
worker_summary: Session fan-out now enters the shared guarded dispatcher: internal/registry/dispatch.go holds the extracted Dispatch() (guard -> webhook -> single store write), Handler.deliver delegates to it, and registry.SessionDeliverer routes fan-out through Dispatch in blocking mode so a transcript outcome describes delivery rather than queue admission. title: [P0] Crier control-panel completion loop — definition of done and the iteration contract
reasoning:
Owner directive (Bane, 2026-10-19): run an autonomous repair/verify loop — add subgoals, get the tasks done, re-run the quorum review, repeat — until the chat UI is complete as a real operator control panel and the bridge claims are true.

THIS ROW IS THE LOOP'S CONTRACT. Each iteration: (1) take the highest-priority pending row below it; (2) dispatch ONE worker into an isolated worktree on branch wt/<id> with a self-contained brief and explicit acceptance criteria; (3) the coordinator verifies the worker's claim by copying nothing on faith — build, vet, full test suite, targeted live probe, diff review; (4) merge only on that evidence, push both remotes and verify by ancestry plus file-in-tree; (5) redeploy the ui-test image and re-run the browser flows when the change is user-visible; (6) re-run a 3-seat quorum on the landed diff and file any NEW gap as a row with acceptance criteria; (7) close the row only when its acceptance criteria are demonstrated, not when a commit exists.

DONE means ALL of: DF-CRIER-328 (session sends travel the guarded transport) landed and proven with a real webhook receiver; DF-CRIER-329 (battery proves execution, not transit) landed; DF-CRIER-330 (truthful A2A terminal states) landed; DF-CRIER-331 (membership, task claim/complete, pinned zone, no-recipient warning) landed; DF-CRIER-332 (identity survives reload by opt-in) landed; DF-CRIER-333 (browser access under CR_AUTH_TOKEN) resolved by the owner's chosen mechanism and proven with an authenticated browser session; DF-CRIER-334 (spec drift) closed; the responsive checks at 390/768/1280 green on the final image with screenshots committed; and a final quorum review with no CONTRADICTED verdict on a must-fix claim.

STOPPING RULES: stop and ask only for a decision that is genuinely the owner's (auth mechanism for browser access; anything that changes the public contract). A worker that stalls without a commit is a failed iteration — re-dispatch with a narrower brief or do it directly, never leave the row in_progress with no evidence. Never claim a row done from a commit, a test name, or a green badge: the artifact must be exercised.
